channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: The Saudi Airline That Launched Right in the Middle of a War
item.description: Violence aimed at civilian aviation has roiled a company that hoped to be a major lever in the kingdom’s long-term economic ambitions.

item.title: She Fled Maduro’s Regime. Washington Brought Her Back to Negotiate With It.
item.description: Dinorah Figuera is leading U.S.-backed talks on Venezuela’s democratic future, even as Trump embraces the officials she wants to replace.

item.title: Power Outages Leave Kyiv Dreading Its Worst Winter of the War
item.description: Some are leaving the Ukrainian capital as Russia intensifies its campaign targeting the country’s energy infrastructure.

item.title: Ukraine’s Military Starlink Is Working Again, Kyiv Says
item.description: Elon Musk addressed the issue, saying Ukrainian military violated Starlink’s terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes.

item.title: Hundreds of Thousands Protest Across France as Clashes Erupt in Paris
item.description: The demonstrations drew large crowds but were less violent than those last weekend.

item.title: FBI Explores Espionage Case Against Saudi OpenAI Suspect
item.description: Engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan was accused of bugging a restricted conference room at the company’s offices.

item.title: U.S. Evacuates Mideast Outposts After Suspected Iranian Plot to Target Americans
item.description: The intelligence has come as the Trump administration prepares to restart military operations against Tehran.

item.title: U.S. Allies Race to Escape SpaceX’s Orbit
item.description: Elon Musk’s blindsiding of Ukraine has spurred efforts by Europe and Canada to roll out satellites under their own control.

item.title: Aboard USS George Washington as It Rearms for Possible Iran Strikes
item.description: Watch as sailors in the USS George Washington strike group prepare for a possible escalation in fighting on the front lines of the Iran war.

item.title: Lula, a Giant of Latin America’s Left, Fights for One Last Shot at Power
item.description: The Brazilian president has an uphill battle to revive his once-magnetic hold on voters.

item.title: The Yellow Vests Are Back on the Streets of France in Test for Government
item.description: The movement that paralyzed Paris eight years ago is joining a widening collection of protest groups challenging authorities.

item.title: Iran Is Now Losing Overland Trade Routes to U.S. Pressure
item.description: Pakistan and Iraq have shut some border crossings, tightening the economic squeeze of the U.S. Navy blockade and air sanctions.

item.title: Moody’s Keeps France’s Credit Rating Unchanged
item.description: Moody’s Ratings kept France’s credit rating unchanged, despite a steady rise in its debts and the political fragmentation that has made it difficult to rein in borrowing.

item.title: Oil Prices Rise on Fears of Middle East Conflict Escalation
item.description: Oil prices closed out the week solidly higher with the market on edge about the possibility of renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and further attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

item.title: Gunman Kills One Near Paris in Suspected Attack on Immigrant Communities
item.description: Authorities detained a suspect and are investigating whether the shootings, which wounded four other people, targeted a specific race, origin or religion.

item.title: Netanyahu Calls for West Bank Lockdown After Deadly Attack
item.description: Two Israeli soldiers were killed in a firefight with Palestinian attackers who were also gunned down.

item.title: Gunmen Kill Seven in Church Attack in Jordan
item.description: Authorities said the shooting that targeted the country’s minority Christian population was an act of terrorism.

item.title: Ukraine Says Starlink Isn’t Working, Despite Trump’s Promise to Restore It
item.description: Soldiers and government officials say connections continued to fail if drones fly at high speeds.

item.title: Trump Called Musk and Asked Him to Lift Ukraine Starlink Restrictions
item.description: Ukrainian officials said that the system remains throttled and that their questions have gone unanswered.

item.title: Venezuela’s Shrimp King Wanted His $700 Million Firm Back. Now He’s in Jail.
item.description: The country’s biggest seafood company shows how Nicolás Maduro’s antibusiness tactics prevail under the U.S.-backed government in Caracas.
